- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.7), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% higher), check for sentiment lag: if sentiment is positive but price drops, model may be overconfident; adjust downward.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% lower), check for sentiment lag: if sentiment is negative but price rises, model may be underconfident; adjust upward.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 5 days, adjust forecast upward by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
